result.summary: The image shows a signalized intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on all visible corners. While basic infrastructure is present, the wide roadway and lack of pedestrian refuge islands or curb extensions increase exposure for people crossing.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: Pedestrians must cross a wide expanse of asphalt without a median or refuge island, increasing exposure time to traffic.
hazards.location_in_image: Across the main roadway (Rising Sun Ave)

hazards.name: Sightline Obstruction
hazards.description: Vehicles parked close to the intersection may obscure pedestrians from the view of approaching or turning drivers.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Intersection Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces closest to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval (LPI)
interventions.description: Program traffic signals to give pedestrians a 3-7 second head start before vehicles get a green light.

result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility continental crosswalk markings and overhead traffic signals, providing a basic level of pedestrian infrastructure. However, the lack of visible pedestrian-specific signal heads and the presence of parked cars near the crossing point create potential visibility and timing hazards.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction from Parked Vehicles

hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, immediately adjacent to the crosswalk.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible on the signal poles, which can lead to confusion regarding crossing phases and clearance intervals.
